name: foobar2000
summary: The audiophile music player runs through Wine with playback, library, tagging, converter and most components.
notes:
foobar2000 (v1.6 32-bit and the 64-bit v2.x builds) installs and runs through Wine: playback of MP3/FLAC/OGG/Opus/AAC/WAV/APE/DSD, the media library, playlists, ReplayGain scanning, tagging, the Converter (using its own bundled encoders or ones you copy into the C:\ drive), the equaliser and most third-party components (foo_* DLLs). Audio goes through Wine's PulseAudio/PipeWire driver; if you hear crackling, raise the buffer in Preferences > Playback > Output (500-1000 ms) or pick 'DS: Primary Sound Driver'.
Not working / not needed: WASAPI-exclusive output components, Windows Media Foundation decoders (use the built-in ones), the 'Send to' shell integration. Files on your Linux disk are under Z:\ (Z:\home\<you>\Music).
The portable install mode is handy: pick 'Portable' in the installer and everything (config, components) stays inside one folder in the C:\ drive.
Native alternatives on Lindos: Strawberry, Quod Libet, DeaDBeeF (the closest in spirit), Rhythmbox.

alternatives.name: DeaDBeeF
alternatives.how: native, foobar2000-like player: Flatpak music.deadbeef.player or the deb from deadbeef.sourceforge.io
